claims.text: Conventionally processed Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 has limited amorphous retention after solidification.
Conventionally processed Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits a complex and unstable thermal response during reheating.
Melt spinning at higher wheel speeds can produce a solidification cooling rate above 10^5 K/s.
Increasing the cooling rate by melt spinning will improve amorphous retention in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 relative to conventional processing.
Increasing the cooling rate by melt spinning will improve the reheating thermal stability of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 relative to conventional processing.
Rapid quenching suppresses the nucleation of crystalline phases.
Rapid quenching suppresses the growth of crystalline phases.
Suppressing crystalline nucleation and growth promotes a homogeneous amorphous structure.
A higher cooling rate reduces the time available for atomic rearrangement and crystallization.
Reduced atomic rearrangement and crystallization during cooling stabilize the amorphous phase.
The proposed stabilization will delay or suppress exothermic crystallization events during reheating.
Rapidly melt-spun Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 will have a higher amorphous-phase fraction immediately after solidification than the slower-cooled baseline.
Rapidly melt-spun Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 will display fewer or delayed DSC exothermic peaks relative to the slower-cooled baseline.
The intervention will succeed only if the cooling rate exceeds a critical rate needed to bypass crystallization kinetics.
The improvement may not be observed when the cooling rate is below the critical threshold.
The improvement may not be observed when reheating rates are high.
